summary: Up slightly from w10 (8.2). The post-w10 fixes landed. The stowed gooseneck heads now hang near-vertical at mid-back, parallel and separate (q14: heads at 0.42 of the back height against 0.44 in py_37301; no crossed V in q13 / q14 / p1 / p4). The seat-pan frame under the backs is dark slate. The fabric saturation gap is gone: back cloth S 0.18-0.20 (q14 / q13 / p8) against 0.17-0.20 in py_37301, hue 220 against 218-219. The flap aspect is 0.87 in q14 against 0.90 in py_37301, and the colour is #445179 S0.44 against #4c6193 S0.48. Ear petal contrast (p90-p10)/p50 is 0.79 against 0.88 in py_37305. Silhouette, headrest, shell, screen and console all read as the ANA ZIM seat. It is still not 8.5, for three reasons, all checked against the SANspotter 2023 photos downloaded this round. (1) The literature pocket is the wrong layout and too wide. In b_san_26 it is an open recessed tray about 0.66 of the screen-frame width. Its dark interior and contents show through the top 45 %, and a smile-shaped tray rim sits about 60 % down with curved black mesh below. Ours is a solid grey bulge 0.94 of the frame width, with the smile at the top and a straight tilted black band that still reads as a ledge (p2 / p6 / p7). (2) Close up, the back cloth is a Lego mosaic of hard-edged flat rectangles (q13b foreground, q14 right edge, p5). Real cloth at that range (py_37305) shows soft woven streaks with thread texture. (3) The gooseneck hose is a thin cable: diameter 13 mm, 0.34 of the head. In b_san_26 and py_37305 the braided hose is 0.5-0.67 of the head diameter. Smaller items: the console front is still more saturated than in py_37306 / 37303; the flap grain is about 2x the photo; the ear petals are rice grains, not sakura chips; the placards are blank (handed off).
lighting_note: Fabric luminance is low in all views: p50 113 (studio p8) and 134-140 (q13 / q14) against 170-175 in py_37301. A hard sun diamond still falls on the 26A-row middle seat back in q14. Both belong to the lighting loop and are not counted against PY. Colours were judged from studio hue and saturation, which match.

issues.issue: The literature pocket has the wrong layout and is about 40 % too wide. In the real seat (b_san_26 crop 330-870 x 540-900; b_san_20) the pocket is an open recessed tray. Its width is about 305 px against the 465 px screen frame (0.66, so about 0.27 m). The top of the tray is open: the dark back recess and the contents show for the upper ~45 %. A darker smile-shaped tray rim (ends high, centre low) sits about 60 % down, and black mesh fills the curved bottom below it. The model has a 0.38 m bucket (0.94 of the 0.405 m frame) with a solid grey bulge. The smile lip is at the top, and a straight black band tilted 16 deg still reads as a ledge from the side (p7, dark sliver aft of the bucket at x 115-140, y 160-190).

issues.fix: src/09b_py.js literature block (py0 = 0.40). Scale x by 0.72: loft SEC widths 0.30/0.36/0.38/0.38/0.37 -> 0.22/0.26/0.275/0.275/0.27; lip polyline x +-0.19 -> +-0.135; recess gRBox 0.40 -> 0.30; stitched edges 0.38 -> 0.27. Move the smile lip from py0+0.185 down to py0+0.075, keeping the 0.015 centre dip but inverted so the ends are high. Lower the loft's top two sections (SEC(0.14..), SEC(0.18..)) to depth 0.012 / 0.006 so the upper pocket is a flat recess. Turn the old top mouth-shadow box (#1e2024, 0.35 x 0.014) into a 0.25 x 0.09 dark quad (#2a2d33) at py0+0.13, dz 0.012, as the open recess. Replace the net gBox with a 4-point curved strip: gTube over x = [-0.13, -0.065, 0, 0.065, 0.13] at y = py0+0.03+0.012*(x/0.13)^2, r 0.022, with LAYER.grille, colour #2a2d31. Net geometry is about the same.

issues.issue: Close up, the back and cushion cloth reads as a Lego/pixel mosaic: flat, uniformly filled, hard-edged white and charcoal rectangles 20-60 px wide (q13b foreground headrest top, q14 right-edge back, p5 cushions). At the same range, py_37305 and py_37306 (cushion at right) show soft-ended woven streaks with visible thread lines and irregular edges. This is the most eye-catching artefact in q13b.
issues.evidence: q13b_pyBacks.png region 0-930 x 340-470. p5_console.png cushions against py_37305 lower right (500-700 x 460-570) and py_37306 (680-930 x 340-575). The tile is 256 px per 0.163 m (1.57 px/mm), so dash edges are 1-px steps magnified about 25x at 0.3 m.
issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py synth_py_back: taper each dash horizontally (ends ramp over 25 % of its length with a cosine, not a hard step). Add a per-dash horizontal streak modulation, multiplying each dash by 0.75-1.0 along 1-2 px sub-rows, so the dash splits into 2-3 threads. Re-cut tex_py_back.png. Better, in src/03_tex.js LAYER pyFleck (17), add a procedural high-frequency weave term in tile UV: lum *= 1 + 0.10*sin(uv.y*2pi*240)*sin(uv.x*2pi*60 + 2*sin(uv.y*2pi*30)), plus 0.06 value noise at 2x tile frequency. That adds about 0.7 mm thread lines that appear only when magnified, and fade with derivatives/mip (fwidth-based fade) so the cabin distance is unchanged. No geometry cost.

questions: The SANspotter 2023 photos (b_san_26 / b_san_20) show the literature pocket as an open recessed tray about 0.27 m wide with a low smile rim and curved mesh, much narrower than the screen. Is that the pocket on every PY seat back, or only on some rows? (Rows 26-27 are in these photos.)
The console colour differs between official photos: py_37301 is distinctly blue (S0.43), py_37306 and py_37303 are dark slate grey (S0.15-0.25). Which one should the model follow?
